title: The chtypes binding parity contract, machine-readable
about: This file is the ONE machine-readable source of truth for what every binding must expose. spec/bindings.md is the prose that explains why; this is what the four test suites actually run against, and scripts/check-parity-doc.sh asserts the two agree on the object-model table.

Each entry is a LOGICAL capability, not a name. The four columns are that capability's spelling in each language, and a spelling that follows the language's own idiom (CompileDDL / compile_ddl / compileDdl / compile) is the point, not a divergence. What must never drift is which capabilities exist and, where a `value` is given, what they answer.
A binding that genuinely should not have a capability declares it as {"absent": "<why>"}. An absent with no reason fails the manifest's own integrity check, so a gap cannot be recorded silently.

The `unlisted` map is the other half of the contract: public names a binding exports that the others deliberately do not need. Each one carries a reason, the no-undeclared-surface check fails on anything that is neither a capability spelling nor listed there, and an entry naming something the binding no longer exports fails too — an excuse with nothing behind it hides the next real gap.

Spelling grammar. go: `Name` for a package-level func/type/const/var, `Type.Name` for a method or exported struct field. python: a dotted path resolved from the `chtypes` package. ts: a dotted path resolved from the package index, `Class.method` meaning a prototype method. rust: `name` for a crate-root item, `Type::name` for an inherent method, `module::NAME` for a module constant, `Enum::Variant` for a variant.

groups.registry: The artifact-directory loader and version dispatch (spec/bindings.md §The object model, §Version selection).
groups.library: One loaded version, and what it can be asked (§The object model, §Introspection, §Teardown).
groups.schema: A compiled column list and the row calls over it (§The object model, §One compile function).
groups.filter: The revision 3/4 filter and block surface (§Revision 3, §Revision 4).
groups.results: The result types every binding hands back (§Result types).
groups.vocabulary: Shared value sets. These carry a `value`: the four bindings must answer with the same bytes, not merely have a symbol.
groups.errors: The refusal/decline split and the artifact error family (§Conformance rule 12, docs/fetch.md §6).
groups.discovery: The three canonical connect-time queries and their parsers (§Discovery).
